title: Qvizz: choose the theme
question: Five themes for Qvizz, each shown as the big-screen question view. Pick one to take into full screen designs, or re-roll.

options.label: Game Night
options.lineage: family board-game box: board, card deck, pawns, plastic pieces
options.thesis: The big screen is the game board: questions are cards drawn from a deck, players are pawns racing along the score track.
options.viewport: A cobalt board with a score track across the top carrying each player's face as a pawn; a white question card dealt from a red deck; four plastic answer tiles in red, green, blue, yellow.
options.risk: Can tip into a kids' game if the type and pieces get cute; needs restraint to stay party-for-adults.

raised.raise: Lobby and podium become one box-insert tray: every player sits in their own compartment, pieces outlined, no stray decoration.
Every change is announced before it lands: the next card's edge peeks from the deck before it flips.
The reveal shows how the room voted as stacks of chips on each answer tile, readable from the back row.
Progress through the quiz is a growing pile of played cards at the side, not a counter.
Each player keeps one pawn colour everywhere: lobby, track, leaderboard, podium and their phone.

options.label: Pub Quiz Night
options.lineage: the local pub quiz: chalk A-board, beer mats, scribbled answer sheets
options.thesis: The ritual everyone already knows: the quizmaster's chalkboard, with beer mats as answer tokens.
options.viewport: A chalkboard in a wood frame; question chalked large; four beer mats ringed in coloured chalk carry A-D; timer chalked top right.
options.risk: The most familiar of the five; chalk texture can soften on a washed-out projector.

options.label: Exercise Book
options.lineage: school squared notebook, highlighters, sticky notes, red-pen marking
options.thesis: The quiz as a school test everyone is finally allowed to enjoy: the drawn faces live in the margin as doodles.
options.viewport: Squared paper with a red margin line; question in ballpoint handwriting; answers highlighted in four colours; the timer on a yellow sticky note.
options.risk: A bright white ground glares on a projector in a dark hall; handwriting faces need care to stay readable.

options.label: Studio 72
options.lineage: 1970s TV game-show set: sunburst wall, contestant podiums, flip-digit scores
options.thesis: Everyone becomes a contestant on a 70s TV quiz show, with their drawn face on the podium name card.
options.viewport: A teal sunburst set; the question on a rounded TV-screen panel with a mustard frame; flip-digit timer; four answer podiums.
options.risk: Retro costume can feel dated if the type leans too hard on 70s lettering.

options.label: Dealt Choices
options.thesis: Answers are dealt as a fan of framed cards above a story window, with a timer bar quietly emptying.
options.viewport: Players' portraits down the left; four answer cards fanned above; the question in a framed window at the bottom with an emptying bar.
options.case: Strong on clarity (the emptying bar, cards that bloom on reveal), weaker on fit: romance-game styling may feel odd at a company party.
options.risk: Reads as a dating-sim pastiche to anyone who knows the genre.

options.label: Reverse-perspective Shelves
options.thesis: Questions as shelf boxes opening toward the viewer.
options.viewport: A cabinet of boxes, the active question box widened.
options.case: Neither friends nor colleagues recognise it; the boxes hide the question.
options.kept: Every player in their own compartment, outlined, no decoration.
options.risk: Obscure and hard to read at speed.

options.label: Live-code Floor
options.thesis: The quiz as code projected on stage.
options.viewport: A code buffer at stage scale.
options.case: A niche tech scene; wrong for mixed party audiences.
options.kept: Announce each change just before it happens.

options.label: Event Display
options.thesis: Every reveal as one frozen collision.
options.case: Spectacular but unrelated to a party quiz.
options.kept: Show how the room voted, honestly, at stage scale.

options.label: Coiled Tower
options.thesis: The quiz rises course by course.
options.case: Slow, earthy; nothing about it says party.
options.kept: Progress shown as a growing physical stack.

options.label: Sleeping City
options.thesis: Each player a district dreaming its own weather.
options.viewport: A night city folding like a blanket.
options.case: Dreamy and calm, the opposite of a buzzing quiz.
options.kept: One colour per player, kept everywhere.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The familiar classroom-quiz look: purple ground, four flat colour blocks, done cleanly.
canonCard.viewport: White question bar, round timer, four colour blocks in a 2x2 grid.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every other quiz app; close to what you have now.
